gaps.title: Unified Data-Driven Career Conversation
gaps.pain: Peruvian students face fragmented, static data across government portals, psychometric tests, and generic AI. No single solution provides a conversational, personalized recommendation that integrates interests, salaries, universities, and regional demand, causing high career mismatch and dropout.
gaps.why_now: Generative AI advances make conversational agents feasible. Datasets like Ponte en Carrera and MiFuturo are available but underutilized. Peruvian youth are digitally native and open to AI guidance, while government open data initiatives provide a reliable foundation.
gaps.evidence_needed: User interviews to confirm frustration with current tools. Prototype engagement metrics (time on task, conversion). Benchmark against ChatGPT's accuracy on local career queries.
gaps.priority: Critical (pain: very high, validation speed: medium, defensibility: high via data integration and vertical tuning)
gaps.risk: ChatGPT may integrate local data via plugins. Government portals could add basic AI. Data licensing/accuracy risks.

gaps.title: Mobile-First, Gen Z Career Exploration Platform
gaps.pain: Official tools are desktop-only, text-heavy, and require active search. Gen Z prefers TikTok/YouTube for career inspiration, which is unstructured and biased. No engaging, on-the-go platform combines entertainment with reliable local career data.
gaps.why_now: Smartphone penetration is high among Peruvian youth. Short-form content consumption is ingrained. Gamification and conversational UI can mimic social media stickiness and reach the majority who avoid traditional portals.
gaps.evidence_needed: Pilot with a mobile prototype; measure daily active users and session length. Compare satisfaction scores vs. Ponte en Carrera. Analyze TikTok career content sentiment.
gaps.priority: High (pain: high, validation speed: fast, defensibility: low-medium without network effects)
gaps.risk: TikTok/Instagram may add career features quickly. High user acquisition cost to build a new habit.

gaps.title: Entry-Level Labor Market Intelligence
gaps.pain: Existing salary data (Ponte en Carrera, LinkedIn) lacks granularity for recent graduates—no differentiation by university prestige, internships, or regional salary variations for junior roles. Students have unrealistic expectations, leading to disillusionment and early career switches.
gaps.why_now: Peru's youth unemployment is rising; informed entry-level choices are critical. Government data is annual and aggregated; no real-time breakdowns exist. AI can model from multiple sources (job boards, surveys).
gaps.evidence_needed: Compare salary ranges from job postings (Bumeran, CompuTrabajo) with Ponte en Carrera. Validate through employer surveys. Check user willingness to share anonymized salary data.
gaps.priority: High (pain: high, validation speed: fast with existing data, defensibility: medium via proprietary aggregation)
gaps.risk: Data gathering may be noisy and requires constant updating. LinkedIn could improve entry-level coverage.

gaps.title: Location-Specific Career Matching
gaps.pain: Peru's labor market varies greatly by region, but government data is national or departmental. Students often migrate without understanding local job prospects. No tool maps career recommendations to specific cities, leading to regional mismatches and unemployment.
gaps.why_now: Regional inequality and internal migration are policy priorities. New open data from MTPS can be parsed. Mobile location data can enhance personalization.
gaps.evidence_needed: Geocode job posting data from major boards. Validate with regional employers. Test user demand for location filters in prototype.
gaps.priority: Medium (pain: high for non-Lima students, validation speed: medium, defensibility: medium—data moat if integrated)
gaps.risk: Government portals might add filters. Data quality poor in some regions.

gaps.title: Scalable, AI-Powered Counselor Alternative
gaps.pain: Human career counselors are scarce, expensive, and often rely on outdated methods. Over 70% of Peruvian students never receive formal guidance. An AI agent can provide instant, 24/7, empathetic support, but trust and accuracy must be proven.
gaps.why_now: ChatGPT has proven conversational AI can simulate empathetic dialogue. Peru's education system is resource-constrained. COVID accelerated acceptance of digital guidance.
gaps.evidence_needed: Track user sentiment and trust scores in conversations. Compare decision satisfaction rates of AI-guided vs. unguided students (longitudinal study needed).
gaps.priority: Medium (pain: very high, validation speed: slow due to outcome measurement, defensibility: low against ChatGPT unless heavily localized)
gaps.risk: ChatGPT's free generic advice may be 'good enough'. Regulatory issues with AI counseling. Parents may distrust machines.

gaps.title: Continuous Career Path Tracking and Adjustment
gaps.pain: Once a career decision is made, there is no feedback loop. High first-year university dropout rates (30%) and later career changes are not systematically addressed. Students lack ongoing guidance to validate or adjust their path.
gaps.why_now: AI can maintain a long-term relationship, using outcome data to refine predictions and suggest pivots. University dropout is a national concern, creating demand for reorientation services.
gaps.evidence_needed: Longitudinal pilot tracking users over 1-2 years. Partner with universities for data sharing. Gauge willingness to share employment outcomes.
gaps.priority: Low (pain: deferred, validation speed: very slow, defensibility: high if proprietary outcomes database built)
gaps.risk: Time to prove value is long. Privacy concerns with tracking individuals.

checkpoint_instruction: Develop a clickable conversational prototype that integrates sample data from MiFuturo and Ponte en Carrera. Conduct 20 user interviews with high school graduates to measure perceived usefulness, trust, and willingness to try the product over existing alternatives.
